findings.scenario: Running the recommended --via-pool memory benchmark against a repository whose FTS extension is unavailable or whose FTS indexes are missing can report PLATEAU and claim that the FTS arena is reclaimed, although no FTS query succeeded.
findings.evidence: Every QUERY_FTS_INDEX rejection is converted to an empty array, and runViaPool returns RSS samples without recording whether FTS ran. The pool intentionally continues when LOAD fails. A focused execution against a temporary LadybugDB with FTS unavailable confirmed QUERY_FTS_INDEX was undefined, yet all six benchmark samples were 173 MB, the machine verdict was PLATEAU, and the benchmark exited 0.
findings.recommendation: Track successful FTS queries in each cycle and require a working FTS workload before emitting CLIMB or PLATEAU. If extension loading fails or all index probes fail, stop with a nonzero exit or an explicit INCONCLUSIVE verdict; skip only individually absent indexes when other FTS probes succeed.
